analysis:
Both units are BASE-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 624-1063), a documentation-only file. The patch only inserts a new v0.10.8 section at the top (head lines 11-333) and renames the v0.10.7 heading. No executable code, keys, protocol handlers, or configuration changed in the supplied evidence, so no security regression can be attributed to these units.

The base text describes pre-existing cluster features: per-tenant prefix-cache scoping with a SHA-256 digest of the cache scope, encrypted SSD prefix tiers, sealed data plane, pair lease handling, and cluster model transfer with manifest pinning. These touch T-041 (prefix cache / TTFT oracle, SEC-035). The base text reads as tightening: requests without a cache scope reuse and keep nothing, and the scope digest is bound into the request fingerprint. It does not loosen the TTL, the account isolation, or the HMAC lookup names.

I saw only a truncated patch excerpt of the new head section, which covers upgrade and rollout notes (same-build pairing refusal, auto-update behavior, the coordinator's 64-approval limit). I could not examine the other new head lines, so claims in them about changed behavior are unverified. The actual code changes (cluster worker, SSD records, model provisioning, coordinator pairing) are outside this batch. A later pass should check that the unseen source matches the changelog claims, especially the SSD tier scoping and quantized records (T-041), model transfer digest pinning, and any cluster registration with the coordinator (TB-002).

No findings. Because the new head section is only partly visible and the code it describes is not supplied, needs_deeper_review is set to true.
